message.content: {"summary":"Your report presents a strong, technically grounded preliminary design, with a clear structure, verified orbit and drag calculations, and STK support. The main gaps are unexplained assumptions in the data budget and contact-time figures, a mismatch between the Vega 700 km orbit and your 600 km design altitude, and some uncited claims. Addressing these would considerably strengthen the technical justification.","next_steps":["Show full working for the ground-contact fraction. 510 s of 771 s is about 66%, not the 'about 60 percent' stated, so correct either the claim or the figure.","Justify the assumptions in Table 6 and Section 2.3. Explain the single 60 km × 1,000 km strip per day, use 2,040 s rather than 2,000 s for the 34-minute eclipse, and calculate eclipse duration and battery sizing from the beta angle at the 08:45 node.","Resolve the Vega altitude mismatch by explaining the 600 km design altitude against the 700 km polar orbit and confirming the dispenser release altitude. Also add references for uncited claims, and derive the lifetime range from the density variation rather than from H/rate alone."],"criteria":{"C1":"You clearly set out the primary mission of imaging the whole Great Barrier Reef at 5 m resolution, why it is needed, why one spacecraft suffices, and who the operator and customers are, including the Marine Park Authority's use of bleaching maps. Your claims are supported by references [1]–[6]. To reach the top band, reference the remaining background claims, such as reef reliance for food and tourism, and tighten the wording of the introduction.","C2":"Your design is thorough and largely accurate. Launch options are compared, the J2 inclination and period are verified, drag decay is reproduced, and the sin β calculation in Section 2.2 is shown. To reach the top band, show working for the 510 s of 771 s contact figure, justify the eclipse duration and battery sizing, explain the 1,000 km strip assumption, and consider more than one ground station.","C3":"Your conclusions recap the key results and identify specific limitations, including Vega C status, 5 m fluid-lensing resolution, the missing X-band link budget and the 45-day mapping time, along with sensible next steps. To reach the top band, link each conclusion more explicitly to your evidence and analyse trade-offs, such as the halving of mapping time with a second satellite in the same plane, rather than largely summarising the body.","C4":"The assessment record for this criterion does not include a full rationale, so no specific strengths or gaps can be confirmed here. The Accomplished descriptor expects a clear engineering structure, consistent formatting, labelled figures and tables, a concise executive summary, and in-text citations that match the reference list. Check your report against each of these points."}}
